Continuing the discussion from Fedora 44 kernel 7.2.5 causes AMDGPU display problems and HDMI failure on ThinkPad T14 Gen 3:

Thank you, Chris, I was happy to see that you had a simple solution. Unfortunately it did not work on my Fedora desktop. It is running Fedora 44, originally installed with Fedora 42.

I did what you suggested:

  1. Boot into a previous kernel (7.2.4)
  2. sudo dnf update --refresh *-firmware (no output)
  3. sudo dnf reinstall kernel* (reinstalled)
  4. sudo reboot
  5. Boot into 7.2.5 kernel

No changes. The UI is still laggy enough to be unusable.

I have also run a normal update afterwards:

sudo dnf upgrade --refresh --offline
sudo dnf offline reboot

posts.name: Chris
posts.cooked:
AP:

Output of lspci | grep AMD:

Your problem can be assumed to be a different one because you do not have an AMD 680M:

AP:

03:00.0 VGA compatible controller: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. [AMD/ATI] Navi 31 [Radeon RX 7900 XT/7900 XTX/7900 GRE/7900M] (rev c8)

Unfortunately, I can currently not take over much more cases. But I add a few tags to make this easier to find for respective experts.

I also update the topic name (maybe you can further refine it?), because the “solution does not work for me” is misleading → as mentioned, I expect you have a different problem.

We have at this time a lot of feedback that the 680M issue is solved, so that’s another indicator that suggests a different issue when it’s not working somewhere. But the key indicator remains that you have no 680M

Also, at first glance, I see you have a lot of external repos: if others have not the issue of yours, one of the external repos`packages might be related. That said, your kernel is obviously not tainted.

My suggestion would be to add more details of your context (incl. what Fedora variant you use, hardware, software, customizations, etc.), what is the exact error, how does it manifest and when, when does it reproduce and when not, and can you get logs? E.g., when 7.2.5 is broken but 7.2.4 works, can you then boot into 7.2.5 (even if all is black), wait some time, force reboot, and then boot back to 7.2.4 and get logs of the previous 7.2.5 boot, or is the then-previous log still 7.2.4? Proper logs would be something from, e.g., sudo journalctl -k --boot=-1 --no-hostname (-1 is the then-previous boot, -k is kernel) and maybe additionally sudo journalctl --boot=-1 --no-hostname (full logs, not only kernel)

Hopefully, someone can take over this case.

AP:
  1. sudo dnf update --refresh *-firmware (no output)

If you tried today, now already some time after this update was pushed to stable, I expect you already had it installed in an earlier update yesterday or the day before. So it is likely not relevant that nothing was found to be updated in that case: the 20260916 you have shown is the current one. So that’s fine.

Just to make sure I understand:

posts.name: Mark
posts.cooked:
AP:
  1. Before running dracut, do I boot into the 7.2.5 kernel?

dracut --force rebuilds the initramfs for the running kernel.
The option --kver some_kernel_version does rebuild for the specified kernel version, not necessarily the current kernel.

  1. I don’t know what exactly you mean with unfreeze, but updates will continue normally. So an upcoming kernel-7.2.7 will be installed once available in the updates repository.

UPDATE: install the 7.2.6 kernel while running the working 7.2.4 kernel. This will prevent the system from removing the 7.2.4 kernel.

accepted_answers.name: Mark
accepted_answers.cooked:
AP:

UPDATE: I tested rebooting to each version 7.1.13 and 7.2.4. The problem is now absent with all kernels.

glad it’s working now. Not sure what went wrong. I guess maybe we reinstalled the el9 packages again while the amdgpu and rocm repositories were still enabled?

You could try investigating with dnf history list and then dnf history info transaction_number as shown by the previous command.

You can do the same for dnf4, they have separate histories.
You might find an install transaction installing files from the amdgpu and rocm repos. Or try to find the initial dnf4 erase transaction initiated via the andgpu-install script.

it’s 1:39 a.m local time. good n8.
